answer.main_body: signboard with post and base block
answer.evidence: Both the upper sign block and the lower base block clearly show horizontal top surfaces (rows 1-5 and rows 19-23, each ~5 rows tall) foreshortened above their vertical south faces, with the post noticeably anchored into the top surface of the base.

The sign board and base are drawn entirely from the front as flat vertical planks (with horizontal plank seam lines at rows 6 and 24). Neither the top edge of the board, the post cut, nor the base shows any foreshortened horizontal top surface (0px).

The top block of the sign clearly displays a foreshortened top surface across rows 1–5 (5 source pixel rows tall), distinct in lighting from the south-facing front face below (rows 6–12). The base also shows its top horizontal surface on rows 20–23.

Both wooden blocks clearly depict top horizontal surfaces in 3/4 view (rows 1-5 for the upper block, rows 19-23 for the lower block surrounding the post) before transitioning to the darker south faces below.
